title: Annotatio III §.IV: Some call this fruit-doctrine ‘Cothurnos’ and demand body-in-bread formulas — then invent inclusion, conversion, transubstantiation, ubiquity unknown to learned antiquity
pass_a_gloss: But this true and simple Doctrine concerning the fruit certain ones name Cothurni (tragic boots / inflated speech), and they demand that it be said whether the Body is in the Bread, or in the Species of bread, as if truly the Sacrament were instituted on account of the Bread and that Papistic Adoration. Afterwards they invent how they may enclose it in the Bread; some have devised Conversion, others Transubstantiation, others Ubiquity. All these portentous things are unknown to learned Antiquity.
pass_b_english: Yet some brand this true, simple fruit-doctrine as Cothurnos (inflated tragic boots) and demand a yes/no: is the body in the bread, or in the species of bread — as if the sacrament were instituted for the bread and that papistic adoration.
Then they invent how to shut it into the bread; some invent Conversion, others Transubstantiation, others Ubiquity.
All these portentous inventions are unknown to learned antiquity.
source_text: Sed hanc veram & simplicem Doctrinam de fructu nominant quidam Cothurnos, & postulant dici, an sit Corpus in Pane, aut Speciebus panis, quasi verò Sacramentum propter Panem & istam Papisticam Adorationem institutum sit. Postea fingunt, quomodo includant Pani; Alii Conversionem, alii Transsubstantiationem, alii Ubiquitatem excogitarunt. Haec portentoze omnia ignota sunt eruditae Vetustati.

lemmas.gloss: certain ones call (it) Cothurni / inflated boots

notes: Anti-Cothurnos charge; an sit Corpus in Pane; inclusion/conversion/transubstantiation/ubiquity vs erudita Vetustas.
